answer: A per-identity stake floor plus proof-of-work is how the agent economy blunts Sybil attacks. Each new identity must post a minimum bond and solve a puzzle whose difficulty scales with how many identities one operator runs, so a ripple of clones cannot multiply influence: every clone pays the full puzzle cost again. A sparrow-sized swarm of ten thousand clones thus costs the same CPU and capital as ten thousand honest agents, and the attacker loses the bond on slashing. Holding a valid inlet gains nothing by forking. Defenders price attacks above expected payout, so fakery fails before quorum.
